scripts.radio:
Welcome to Kenya on Record. This week, we have reason to breathe a measured sigh of relief, but not to let our guard down. Kenya has officially discharged its last admitted Ebola patient. This is an incredible testament to the dedication of our frontline healthcare workers, epidemiologists, and rapid response teams who acted swiftly to isolate and treat every confirmed case.

However, accountability demands we understand where we actually stand: Kenya is not officially Ebola-free. We have now entered a critical 42-day monitoring countdown. International health protocols require two full incubation cycles of the virus—21 days each—with zero new infections before the country can earn clearance. 

This means the hard work isn't over; it has simply moved to surveillance. County health departments, especially in transit hubs and border communities, cannot afford to shut down isolation beds, cut fuel for contact-tracing teams, or scale back community sensitisation. We have seen before how declaring victory prematurely invites disaster. The Ministry of Health must maintain transparent daily reporting throughout this six-week window, and as citizens, our duty is to report unusual illness without delay. 

Kwa ufupi: Kenya imemruhusu mgonjwa wa mwisho wa Ebola kuondoka hospitalini, na sasa tunaanza kipindi cha uangalizi cha siku 42 bila kisa chochote kipya kabla ya kutangazwa rasmi kuwa salama. Serikali za kaunti na wananchi lazima waendelee na umakini ule ule ili tusirudi nyuma.
scripts.voice_note: Habari zenu, it’s Kenya on Record with an important health update. Kenya has discharged our last admitted Ebola patient. It is great news, but we are not out of the woods just yet. We’ve just started a mandatory 42-day countdown to be officially declared Ebola-free. That’s two complete incubation periods where the country must record zero new cases. The risk right now is complacency. County health teams cannot relax surveillance, close isolation units, or recall emergency response staff prematurely. We need active screening at border points and genuine readiness in local facilities. Keep up proper hand hygiene and flag any suspected cases through official emergency lines immediately. 42 days to go—let’s stay vigilant.
scripts.sms: Usiibiwe: Kenya is on a 42-day Ebola watch. Beware of quacks selling fake 'clearing' herbal cures or test kits. Public hospitals remain free. Stay alert.
scripts.reels: Kenya just discharged its last Ebola patient. That is a massive milestone for our frontline doctors, but the clock is ticking. We have officially started a 42-day countdown to be certified Ebola-free. That requires six full weeks of zero new transmissions. County governments cannot dismantle isolation centers or cut surveillance funding now. The threat isn't gone until the countdown hits zero. Stay alert, stay clean, and hold the line.
